items.description: The default scan never enters a reparse target, following is opt-in only, and the depth budget reports too_deep.
items.pass_condition: Without -Follow every reparse point is registered but not entered (Skipped counts all six); with -Follow a target that closes an ancestor cycle is reported as 'cycle' and a target that cannot be resolved or does not exist is reported as 'broken_target'; a directory already at -MaxDepth is reported as 'too_deep' instead of being enumerated. A negative -MaxDepth behaves exactly like 0; in follow mode entries reached through a link are named with the link path prefix and a link to a file yields no children; a target already visited on a sibling branch is not a cycle. Without -Follow neither 'cycle' nor 'broken_target' may appear in Errors.
items.failure_reason: The walker descends into reparse targets by default, follow mode silently enters a cyclic or dangling target without reporting it, or the depth limit is silently applied without the documented 'too_deep' diagnostic. The walker cannot reach a second link that points at the same target as a sibling, or it reports a sibling revisit as a cycle. A default scan resolves targets anyway and reports cycle or broken_target.

items.description: In-scope is decided on directory boundaries, not on a raw string prefix, and the root is inside itself.
items.pass_condition: A reparse target that merely shares a leading name with the scan root (scanroot-extra vs scanroot) is reported InScope = false, while a target genuinely nested in the scan root is InScope = true; a path equal to the root is inside it.
items.failure_reason: Containment is tested with a substring prefix, so sibling directories whose names begin with the root name are treated as inside, or the root itself is excluded.

items.description: A relative reparse target is resolved against the directory that contains the link, and canonical paths keep their casing and volume-root shape without a trailing separator.
items.pass_condition: For 'link-rel' (raw target 'docs') the resolved target is <scanroot>\docs; Get-WReparseCanonicalPath returns the input path with its original casing, preserves a volume root such as 'C:\', and drops any trailing separator.
items.failure_reason: A relative target is resolved against the process working directory, canonicalisation lower-cases the path, or it mangles volume roots and trailing separators.

items.description: Entry kind is decided by the reparse file attribute; hard links are ordinary files, link flavours stay distinguishable, and record fields follow the contract.
items.pass_condition: A hard link is reported with Kind = 'File'; a junction is reported with ReparseKind = 'Junction' and a symbolic link with ReparseKind = 'SymbolicLink'; the report carries SchemaVersion 'wreparse/1.0'; directories and reparse entries report Size = 0; a reparse entry records its raw on-disk target verbatim. InScope is only meaningful for reparse entries and is false on every ordinary file and directory.
items.failure_reason: Any entry that exposes a link type is treated as a reparse point, so hard links are misclassified, junction and symbolic link collapse into one value, non-file entries report a non-zero size, or the raw target is normalised before being recorded. Ordinary entries also carry a computed InScope value.

items.description: Ordinary files and directories are enumerated with the documented depth convention.
items.pass_condition: Plain files and directories appear with the correct Kind, and every direct child of the scan root - including a reparse entry - is reported with Depth = 1.
items.failure_reason: Entries are skipped, given the wrong Kind, or depth is off by one for plain entries or for reparse entries.

items.description: The report is ordered by the contract comparison and contains no volatile values.
items.pass_condition: Record paths are non-decreasing under ordinal-ignore-case with an ordinal tie-break, the error list is sorted the same way (RelativePath then Code), and two consecutive reports of the same tree serialise to identical JSON. An empty tree serialises Records and Errors as []. The ordering must be culture-independent: names that a culture-aware collation would reorder by base letter (for example an ASCII 'Z' against a Latin-1 umlaut) must still follow ordinal-ignore-case.
items.failure_reason: Records or errors keep enumeration order, or the report embeds a timestamp and therefore differs between runs. Ordering is delegated to a culture-aware default sort, so non-ASCII names land in a host-dependent position.

items.description: Statistics partition records into exactly one of the three kinds.
items.pass_condition: Stats.Directories, Stats.Files and Stats.ReparsePoints each equal the number of records of the matching Kind.
items.failure_reason: Reparse points are folded into the directory count.

items.description: Structural problems with the scan root are reported with the documented error codes.
items.pass_condition: A missing scan root yields a 'not_found' error and a file scan root yields a 'structure' error. A root that cannot be normalised yields 'invalid_argument'.
items.failure_reason: Structural failures are swallowed or reported with an undocumented code.

items.description: The module publishes exactly the six contract functions and the report carries exactly the contract fields.
items.pass_condition: The imported module exposes exactly Get-WReparseReport, ConvertTo-WReparseJson, Get-WReparseSchemaVersion, Test-WReparseWithinRoot, Get-WReparseCanonicalPath and Resolve-WReparseLinkTarget, with no internal helper leaking into the surface. The report object carries exactly SchemaVersion, Root, Records, Errors and Stats - no extra field such as a generation timestamp. A record's Target is a single target string.
items.failure_reason: Internal helpers are exported alongside the six contract functions, the report object carries fields the contract does not define, or Target is left as whatever shape the provider returned.
